GAP-SUPERSEDE.title: A new note does not retire the old one
GAP-SUPERSEDE.summary: OneMemory has no 'supersedes' link between notes, and search does not prefer the newer of two notes about the same fact. Correcting a note in place works (the old value is gone). Writing a second note and leaving the first alone returns both, in relevance order.

GAP-RECENCY.title: A flagged-stale note can still rank above a fresher one
GAP-RECENCY.summary: Staleness is a flag plus a mild ranking penalty (x0.95 per 90 days). A 200-day-old note whose words match the query better still ranks first; the flag is on it, but the current value is not first.

GAP-HISTORY.title: No version history of note bodies
GAP-HISTORY.summary: An edit replaces the body. The change feed keeps titles, writers and times but not earlier text, so after a bad overwrite (or an overwrite followed by distrusting the overwriter) the trusted original cannot be recovered from OneMemory itself. Backups are the only way back.

GAP-REST-CAS.title: REST updates have no compare-and-swap
GAP-REST-CAS.summary: The MCP tool state_write accepts if_rev and refuses an edit made on an out-of-date copy. The REST PUT /notes/:id ignored it, so a stale REST edit silently replaced a newer one. Fixed in 1.5.0: PUT now takes if_rev and answers 409.

GAP-CONFIDENCE.title: No confidence field
GAP-CONFIDENCE.summary: A note has no confidence value. A client may send one, but the server drops it silently and nothing can rank, filter or flag notes by how sure the writer was.
